solution: $\log_B A=\dfrac{1}{\log_A B}$, so the equation is $\log_A B=\dfrac{1}{\log_A B}\Rightarrow(\log_A B)^{2}=1\Rightarrow B=A$ or $AB=1$
solution_full: Write $A=x^{2}+4x+2$ and $B=4x+6$. Both logarithms are defined only when $A>0,\ A\neq1,\ B>0,\ B\neq1$.
$B>0\Rightarrow x>-\dfrac32$. $A>0\Rightarrow x<-2-\sqrt2$ or $x>-2+\sqrt2$; with $x>-\dfrac32$ this leaves $x>\sqrt2-2$.
$A=1\Rightarrow x^{2}+4x+1=0\Rightarrow x=-2\pm\sqrt3$; only $x=\sqrt3-2$ lies in $x>\sqrt2-2$. $B=1\Rightarrow x=-\dfrac54<\sqrt2-2$.
So the domain of the equation is $D=\left(\sqrt2-2,\infty\right)\setminus\left\{\sqrt3-2\right\}$.
Put $u=\log_A B$. By the change of base, $\log_B A=\dfrac{1}{u}$ ($u\neq0$ since $B\neq1$). The equation is $u=\dfrac1u\Rightarrow u^{2}=1\Rightarrow u=1$ or $u=-1$.
$x=-2$: $A=B=-2<0$, not in $D$. $x=2$: $A=B=14$, in $D$; both sides equal $1$.
$2x^{2}+10x+11=0\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{-5\pm\sqrt3}{2}\approx-1.63,\ -3.37$. Both are less than $-\dfrac32$, so $B<0$ (here $A<0$ too, which is why $AB=1$ holds); both rejected.
Hence $S=\left\{2,-\dfrac12\right\}$ and the sum of its elements is $2-\dfrac12=\dfrac32$.
(Ignoring the domain gives all five candidates with sum $-\dfrac{11}{2}$; keeping $x=-2$ gives $-\dfrac12$.)
originality_note: New: a reciprocal-log equation log_A B = log_B A with a quadratic base and a linear argument; the two branches B = A and AB = 1 give a quadratic and a cubic, and three of the five candidates die in the domain (one with A = B negative, two where AB = 1 holds with A and B both negative) (way 5). Closest known: log_x(x+1) = log_{x+1}(x)-type exercises and log equations with a quadratic base. Different because: the AB = 1 branch is a cubic whose rational root survives while its two irrational roots satisfy AB = 1 only through negative factors, so the domain decides the answer.

concept_use.Logarithmic equations with a variable ba: The equation has the variable base x^2+4x+2; change of base turns it into (log_A B)^2 = 1, giving the branches B = A and AB = 1.
concept_use.Domain of algebraic, logarithmic, expone: The domain of the logarithmic expressions (A > 0, A != 1, B > 0, B != 1, i.e. x > sqrt2 - 2, x != sqrt3 - 2) rejects x = -2 and x = (-5 +- sqrt3)/2.

key_step: Reducing log_A B = log_B A to B = A or AB = 1, factoring the cubic and filtering five candidates by the domain.
justification: Two ideas linked: the reciprocal change-of-base step and a domain check that rejects three of five candidates, two of them irrational roots of a cubic that only fail through signs. Comparable to 2023-P2-Q3 (L3), a sum of solutions decided by range care; harder than 2024-P1-Q8 (L2).
